excerpt: Connect Claude (and other MCP-compatible tools) to your Limitless MCP server to search and ask about your Lifelogs.
At this time, ChatGPT's MCP (Connectors) integration works for Pro and Workspace accounts only.
Once you're logged in, you can create an API key by clicking the "Create API Key" button in the top right corner of the screen.
Get recent Lifelogs from your Pendant, search specific date ranges, sort, and paginate.
Search query to perform hybrid search across lifelogs. Hybrid search is a combination of keyword search and semantic search
isStarred boolean Filter entries by their starred status. Optional.
Returns a specific lifelog entry by ID.
Permanently deletes a specific lifelog entry by ID. All associated transcripts, audio, and metadata are fully deleted and cannot be recovered.
Download audio from your Pendant as Ogg Opus files for a specific time range. Returns audio data directly as binary Ogg Opus format without transcoding.
Get your chats (Ask AI conversations) with pagination support. Returns chats with messages, tool calls, and limited information about tool results.
Permanently delete a specific chat by ID. Users can only delete their own chats.
Filter chats created by scheduled prompts. When `true`, only scheduled chats are returned; when `false`, only non-scheduled chats are returned.
We've created an example repository that shows how to use the Developer API to access your data.
Default Rate Limit: 180 requests per minute per API key
We just launched a feature to make it easy to export all of your data.
if you want to delete all of your data, that is also very easy to do within the app.
You'll no longer need to pay a subscription, and existing customers get the Unlimited Plan for free.
you will still be able to access previously recorded meetings throughout 2026.
At launch the Limitless app was overwhelmed. One user reported seeing the error "Sorry! Our app is melting due to overwhelming load Error fetching: TypeError: Load failed".

A big fan of Rewind (despite its battery drain) said its best feature is that everything is verifiably local, and they'd take an inferior AI model over shipping recordings of everything they see and hear to someone else. They called Limitless a hard pass: "I don't care how good the encryption is, sending this kind of thing to anyone's cloud is a nope for me."

One commenter said the product "looks incredible" and the site "looks fantastic," and in a perfect world they'd pre-order immediately. But they refuse to subject friends and family to being recorded, with those recordings going to a cloud they don't control, citing a recent AT&T data leak.

One commenter wants a pendant like this focused on local-only processing (local models or a user-chosen API key, open-source software, open data/API) and would pay over $500 for it. They said they'd never trust a startup with this sort of data, and that anyone in a serious job would almost certainly be unable to use it for work.

Summary of the shift: the company formerly known as Rewind AI is renaming to Limitless, going all-in on a wearable pendant mic, and moving a lot of processing off device and into the cloud. Another user commented that it sounds like this is killing or replacing Rewind.
Trust complaint: the website doesn't make clear who the company is or where it is based. Given how much personal data it wants, the commenter said that should be up front and center.
Criticism of the launch trailer: for a brand-new product category, it spends time showing off colors and finishes instead of what the device does and how to use it in daily life.
After watching the demo video, a user was confused about what "seen" means in the tagline and asked whether the pendant has a camera.
Feature request: a pro feature that lets users upload their own audio.

Skeptic argument: the value of note-taking is the act itself, which builds memory and insight. Users who can't be bothered to take their own notes rarely go back and search through auto-captured voice or LLM-summarized notes, a lesson dictation-as-a-service startups keep relearning.

Concern that over-reliance on the cloud, and the device not interfacing with the phone (where reminders, alarms and messages live), will make pendants like this a tough sell compared with just pulling out a phone.
